title: Exploratory missions
summary: The session walks exploratory missions in its main thread on the controller or drives a declared Test Machine without adding a source checkout. The walking session submits a verdict for each case and cites evidence; unsupported executors refuse with a named recovery. A stopped mission with no product proof settles as mission_setup_blocked with an error verdict and its named prerequisite; diagnostic and restore artifacts do not earn human review. Authors select an OS and any required capability tags for host missions, or OS slots for several hosts; a mission never names a host. A resume keeps execution affinity, while a replacement selects afresh. Order small cross-machine missions after single-host missions. Hostless missions explore on the controller, record a docket without a lease, and need no reset or restore receipt; explicit host declarations retain host custody and starting-state checks. Frozen snapshots ignore stale starting-state declarations on cases that need no Test Machine; plan authoring still refuses those stray fields. Missions ask only for real user actions; browser actions follow the action reference and the full list in yoke qa browser step --help, including grant_clipboard and sign_in. Unusual states use fixtures, seeded identities or component tests rather than walker DOM edits, response overrides or width measurement. Keyboard proof needs a declared Test Machine with the required input support. Phone checks use a phone-sized viewport or the iOS Simulator on a macOS host; no phone Test Machine exists, and a viewport does not prove real-phone touch behavior.
